x: An etymological dictionary traces the history and origin of words; etymology is the study of word origins (not to be confused with entomology, insects).
Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.
Ashwagandha is Withania somnifera (family Solanaceae). Withania coagulans is the 'paneer dodi' (Indian cheese-maker) and Solanum nigrum is black nightshade.

INSAT satellites serve telecommunication, TV broadcasting, meteorology (weather imaging), disaster warning and search-and-rescue, tele-education and telemedicine. Astronomy is not an INSAT application; it is done by science missions such as AstroSat.

Thorndike's multifactor theory of intelligence is called the Anarchic theory (intelligence = many independent abilities). Monarchic/Unitary theory treats intelligence as one power, and Two-factor theory is Spearman's.

Observation (especially controlled/naturalistic observation by others) is an objective method of studying behaviour. Introspection, interview and dream analysis depend on the person's own report, so they are subjective.

Action research is research by practitioners (teachers) into their own problems to improve practice; Stephen Corey (1953) brought it into education and it is the standard method for studying classroom problems. A field experiment tests a hypothesis in a natural setting and is not specific to classroom problems.
source: https://structural-learning.com/post/action-research-in-the-classroom-a-teachers-guide ('Teachers use action research to study classroom problems'; Corey 1953)
evidence: Local library: no line on action research

x: David McClelland (with Atkinson) developed the theory of achievement motivation (need for achievement, affiliation and power). Murray first listed 'need for achievement' among needs, and Maslow gave the need hierarchy.

from_notes: Observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, conclusion, then replication / peer review
x: The scientific method (observation, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, conclusion, replication) is the modern, systematic way of acquiring knowledge; authority, expert opinion and personal experience are traditional sources.

A rocket expels hot gases backward at high speed and the reaction pushes it forward: every action has an equal and opposite reaction (Newton's third law; equivalently conservation of momentum). It needs no air to push against, so it works in space.
source: Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.26: conservation of momentum – 'Recoil of gun, rocket propulsion'

x: Bright colour, scent and nectar are adaptations that attract insects, so such a flower is insect-pollinated (entomophily). Wind- and water-pollinated flowers are small, dull and without nectar or scent.
source: PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.38: 'Insects (Entomophily): insects, attracted by flowers' bright colours, sweet scents, and nectar'

x: Rheology is the study of the flow and deformation of matter, chiefly liquids and soft solids (paints, blood, polymers, dough).
Environmental psychology studies the interplay between people and their physical surroundings (built and natural environments).
Axiology is the branch of philosophy that studies the nature of values, covering ethics (moral values) and aesthetics (beauty).

'Cyber insects' (cyborg insects) are living insects with silicon micro-systems implanted in their bodies, often at the pupal stage, so that their flight can be steered and they can carry sensors for gases or explosives (US DARPA HI-MEMS programme). They are not software viruses or explosives.
source: https://www.jyi.org/2007-july/2007/7/10/insect-cyborg-sentinels (silicon microsystems placed inside the insect during metamorphosis; DARPA HI-MEMS)
evidence: Local library: no line on cyber/cyborg insects

x: Genetic engineering (recombinant DNA technology) manipulates the genes of living organisms, so it is a branch of biology (biotechnology), not of electronics or civil/mechanical engineering.

from_notes: Ethology = study of animal behaviour (Lorenz, Tinbergen, von Frisch – Nobel 1973); etymology = word origins; entomology = insects
x: Ethology is the scientific study of animal behaviour (Lorenz, Tinbergen and von Frisch, Nobel 1973). Etymology is word origins, ecology is organism-environment relations and euphenics is improving the phenotype.

The study of physical geography of past geological ages is palaeogeography, which is a branch of historical geography ('the study of historical geography, generally physical landscapes'), so it is included in historical geography. 'Pa-liography' (palaeography) is the study of ancient writing, and biogeography studies the distribution of living things.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palaeogeography (first sentence: 'the study of historical geography, generally physical landscapes'); OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography (src/geography/onlyias-ncert-human-geography-03.txt) p.8: historical geography = geographies of the past
evidence: PMF Physical Geography Part 1 (src/geography/pmf-physical-geography-01.txt): historical geography = historical processes of space organisation
dispute: Printed key / most books: Historical geography. Strictly the specific branch is palaeogeography (Wikipedia: Palaeogeography), which sits within historical geography.

x: Entomology is the scientific study of insects. Ichthyology is fish, parasitology parasites and malacology molluscs.
Entomology is the study of insects. Ichthyology (fish), parasitology (parasites) and malacology (molluscs) are different fields.

B and C are correct: anatomy describes body structures, and biotechnology uses living cells to make or modify products such as GM foods. A is wrong: astrobiology studies the origin and possibility of life in the universe, while bacteria are studied in bacteriology.
The Indian Navy staged its Operational Demonstration off RK Beach, Visakhapatnam (MILAN-2022 city parade, 27 Feb 2022, and Navy Day, 4 Dec 2022), the home of the Eastern Naval Command.

A 'ticker' (news crawl) is the strip of scrolling text, such as headlines or share prices, along the bottom of a television screen.
A homepage is the main or introductory page of a website, from which its other pages are linked.
ICOLC is the International Coalition of Library Consortia, an informal group of library consortia (since 1997) that discusses licensing of electronic resources.
MBO stands for Management by Objectives, popularised by Peter Drucker (The Practice of Management, 1954): manager and subordinate agree on goals and appraise performance against them.
Goitre is the enlargement of the thyroid gland, mostly due to iodine deficiency.
Apache Solr is an open-source enterprise search platform (built on Lucene) used for full-text indexing and searching, e.g. in library discovery systems.
Datum is the singular of 'data': a single piece of information or fact.
Bitmap (BMP) is a long-established raster image file format that stores an image as a grid of pixels.

Sensation (the raw response of a sense organ to a stimulus) is the simplest form of cognition; perception and concept formation build on it.
